title: Experimental Investigation of Tunable-Order Hilbert-Space Ergodicity
authors: Zou-Wei Pan, Wenquan Liu, Xing Rong
abstract: Hilbert-space ergodicity (HSE) provides a new framework for studying thermalization in driven quantum systems, complementing the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, which is restricted to static systems. This ergodicity is hierarchical: by quantifying how randomly the dynamics explores the Hilbert space, one obtains a family of levels termed $k$-HSE. While HSE has been observed at the lowest and highest levels, finite-order HSE dynamics remains largely unexplored due to the difficulty of constructing such drives. Here, we explore this intermediate regime and uncover its distinctive physics. We first propose and prove that a family of $m$-tone drives on qubits realizes $k$-HSE up to $k = 2m{-}3$, with drive parameters determined at $O(k)$ cost. Using a single nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond, we verify this design by showing that a 3-tone drive realizes 3-HSE, with fourth-order statistics depending on the initial state. Further in-depth theoretical analysis shows that this initial-state dependence is generic across drives, demonstrating the possibility of recovering the initial state from higher-order statistics even when the dynamics is ergodic. Our work broadens the study of quantum ergodicity and reveals intriguing physics within its hierarchy.
summary: This paper explores Hilbert-space ergodicity (HSE) in driven quantum systems, proposing a theoretical framework and experimental realization using NV centers in diamond. The authors show that specific multi-tone drives can achieve tunable $k$-HSE, while also revealing that initial-state information can persist in higher-order statistical moments even when the system appears ergodic at lower orders.
main_problem: The paper investigates Hilbert-space ergodicity (HSE), a framework for studying thermalization in driven quantum systems that extends beyond static systems studied by ETH.
main_result: They demonstrate that specific $m$-tone drives can realize $k$-HSE up to $k=2m-3$, and crucially, they show that initial-state information survives in higher-order statistics ($\Delta(4)$) even when lower-order ergodicity is achieved.
method: The study combines theoretical proofs showing the construction of $k$-HSE drives with experimental verification using a nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond to measure temporal moments.
model_or_system: The theoretical model involves designing $m$-tone quasiperiodic drives on qubits. Experimentally, the platform is a single nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond, where the qubit is encoded in the spin-1 electronic ground state.

important_parameters: The order of ergodicity, $k$, is tunable by the number of tones, $m$, up to $k=2m-3$. The initial state dependence is quantified by the angle $\gamma$ between the initial state vector and the first drive axis.
main_assumptions: The theoretical analysis assumes the limit of the trace distance equals the trace distance of the limit. Experimentally, state reconstruction relies on measuring photoluminescence rates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the concept of $k$-HSE decay, showing $\Delta(k)$ vanishing for low $k$ but plateauing at a non-zero, initial-state-dependent value for higher $k$. The NV center setup and pulse sequences are also detailed.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces HSE as a complement to ETH, then theoretically proposes and proves the construction of $k$-HSE drives. This is followed by experimental verification using the NV center, culminating in a detailed analysis of the initial-state dependence of higher-order statistics.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally verifiable mechanism (tunable drives) to probe the hierarchy of quantum ergodicity, offering deep insights into how memory of initial conditions can persist in complex, driven quantum dynamics.

(a) Analogous to clas- sical ergodicity, HSE describes the property that quantum dy- namics uniformly explores the Hilbert space in the long-time limit. (b)–(c) Comparison between HSE at infinite order (b, CHSE) and at finite order (c, k-HSE). A distinctive feature of k-HSE dynamics is that initial-state information survives in the statistics of order k+1 and higher. (d) A qubit example, with the model specified in the text. Here (θ, ϕ) denote the polar and azimuthal angles of the initial state.

FIG. 2. Realizing tunable HSE with m-tone drives. (a) Design of the drive: a sequence of m rotations about dis- tinct axes Hj = nj·σ, with rationally independent frequencies {ωj}. (b) Progressively realizing higher-order HSE by adding rotation axes and tuning their angles. The rows labeled by ℓ represent the ℓ-th HSE equation in Eq. (3). Each equation is fulfilled by adjusting ϕj = ∠(nj, nj+1) with satisfied condi- tions indicated by colored cells. The number of consecutively colored cells counted from the top determines the k-HSE or- der of the m-tone drive. Notably, setting ϕ1 = π/2 satisfies all odd rows. Each even row is then filled by adding one ad- ditional rotation axis at a time, so...
